$comment: Which Swift symbol carries each design-scale.json token's value. The web copies are generated (webviews/scripts/pages/gen-design-scale.mjs); the Swift ones are hand-written, so scripts/cmux-next/check-design-scale-parity.py reads both and fails when a mapped pair differs, when a DesignTokens constant has no pair here, or when a drift entry is no longer true (a drift entry can only be removed: fix the value and delete it). A pair compares, it pins no number: change the token and its Swift symbol together. `schema` is a path into design-scale.json (`list[name=x].field`); `read` turns that value into the Swift unit: `px` (the number), `percent` (the number / 100), `blurPx` (N of blur(Npx)), `fallbackPx` (N of var(--x, Npx)), `nth:K` (the K-th number of a string, 0-based). `swift` is FILE:SYMBOL (a `let`/`var` with a literal, a DesignTokens alias, or SYMBOL.field of an Elevation(...) call). `optional` pairs may be absent on both sides (a pair a lane adds), never on one.

drift.reason: the button corner moved to the tab's (Metrics.buttonCornerRadius, namedRadii control's 8 px fallback; Lawrence 2026-11-12) and this constant kept radii md's 6; nothing reads DesignTokens.radiusControl
the chrome glass level moved to 62 in the schema; this constant kept the old 60 and nothing reads DesignTokens.glassPlainTint

unmapped.reason: computed (Metrics.surfaceCornerRadius, a density tunable), no literal to read
computed from the tab corner (density token tabCornerRadius, Chrome's ratio on the tab height), not a literal; namedRadii control's 8 px is only the web fallback
no design-scale token names the tooltip corner; webviews/test/tooltip-metrics.test.ts holds it against desktop.css --tooltip-radius
namedRadii menu is a var() with no px; schemas/menu-metrics and gen-menu-metrics.py own it
the dialog corner is computed (button corner plus padding); no design-scale token until dialog.padding lands
Tunable<Double>.number(...) defaults per density; not a single literal
check-surface-roles.py already holds them to schemas/surface-roles and design-scale glassMaterial
